bounds.domain: Two immutable original object keys, one deletion root and two lease generations. Successful idempotent delete, lost replies, takeover and cursor acknowledgement are separate transitions.
bounds.atomicity: Final SQL publication atomically retains all original manifests in v2 job.data and marks app metadata deleted. Small result cursors require original live job lease; v2 job/org deletion waits for cleanup confirmation. Legacy v1 jobs retain prior semantics and may have orphan debt.
bounds.conformance: Twenty-three real PGlite object/service cases and ten PostgreSQL cases, including independent connection contention, job/org cascade protection and post-lock expiry in UTC, New York and Kathmandu. Provider effects are local controlled fixtures.
bounds.gaps: Assumes original R2 binding and immutable deployment-key ownership remain stable; no live R2, bucket rotation, remote atomicity, arbitrary-count proof or general TypeScript refinement is established. A timed-out in-flight exact-key delete may finish after lease loss. Complete plans intentionally remain inline and immutable in job.data, with small independently updated result receipts. Physical PostgreSQL write-cost measurements are experimental evidence, not a worst-case bound. Uploads bind their complete plan before PUT; deletion waits for the original writer to acknowledge all issued PUTs and stop issuing more. Ambiguous legacy/failed uploads remain typed recovery-required; no elapsed-time quiescence or automatic unknown-PUT recovery is claimed.
bounds.progress: Progress requires eventual provider/SQL availability, retained original queue, fair scheduling, and a successful acknowledged attempt before bounded no-progress retries exhaust. This safety model does not prove temporal liveness. Forward progress resets the bounded retry counter; one invocation handles at most 64 objects.
